title: Mzilikazi's migration
span: c. 1822 to 1868, from Zululand to Zimbabwe
summary: Mzilikazi broke with Shaka and led his followers more than a thousand kilometres north, building the Ndebele kingdom on the move. It ended in present-day Zimbabwe, around Bulawayo.
caveat: The record draws on Ndebele oral tradition and the journals of missionaries and travellers who met Mzilikazi. Many of his early settlements are known only approximately.

stops.title: Breaks with Shaka
stops.narration: Mzilikazi, a Khumalo chief serving Shaka, kept cattle from a raid instead of handing them over. Expecting punishment, he fled north with a few hundred followers.
stops.confidence_note: The year and the starting point are approximate.
sources: R. Kent Rasmussen, Migrant Kingdom: Mzilikazi's Ndebele in South Africa (1978)

stops.title: On the Steelpoort
stops.narration: His followers settled for a few years in the east of the Highveld, raiding and absorbing local communities. The kingdom grew as captives and refugees joined.
stops.confidence_note: The marker shows the general area of these early settlements.
sources: R. Kent Rasmussen, Migrant Kingdom: Mzilikazi's Ndebele in South Africa (1978)

stops.title: Settles near the Magaliesberg
stops.narration: The Ndebele moved west and built towns in the Magaliesberg area. In 1829 the missionary Robert Moffat visited, beginning a long friendship with Mzilikazi.
stops.confidence_note: The marker shows Hartbeespoort; his towns lay across this region.
sources: R. Kent Rasmussen, Migrant Kingdom: Mzilikazi's Ndebele in South Africa (1978)
The Matabele Journals of Robert Moffat (1945)

stops.title: Moves to Mosega
stops.narration: Pressed by raids from Zulu and Griqua forces, Mzilikazi moved further west to the Marico valley, with Mosega as a main centre.
stops.confidence_note: The marker shows Zeerust; Mosega lies nearby.
sources: R. Kent Rasmussen, Migrant Kingdom: Mzilikazi's Ndebele in South Africa (1978)

stops.title: Battle of Vegkop
stops.narration: Ndebele regiments attacked a Voortrekker wagon laager here and were driven off by gunfire, though they took most of the trekkers' cattle.
sources: R. Kent Rasmussen, Migrant Kingdom: Mzilikazi's Ndebele in South Africa (1978)

stops.title: Driven from Mosega
stops.narration: Voortrekker and Griqua forces attacked Mosega in January and again later in the year. Mzilikazi decided to leave the Highveld and lead his people north across the Limpopo.
sources: R. Kent Rasmussen, Migrant Kingdom: Mzilikazi's Ndebele in South Africa (1978)

stops.title: A new kingdom
stops.narration: After the migration split and rejoined, the Ndebele settled on the highlands of south-western Zimbabwe, conquering and absorbing Shona and other communities there.
stops.confidence_note: His capitals moved over time; the marker shows Bulawayo.
sources: R. Kent Rasmussen, Migrant Kingdom: Mzilikazi's Ndebele in South Africa (1978)

stops.title: Buried in the Matobo Hills
stops.narration: Mzilikazi died after nearly 50 years as king and was buried in a cave at Entumbane in the Matobo Hills. His son Lobengula succeeded him.
stops.confidence_note: The marker shows the Matobo hills; the grave site lies within them.
sources: R. Kent Rasmussen, Migrant Kingdom: Mzilikazi's Ndebele in South Africa (1978)
